walkthroughs.body_html:
Charles Darwin proposed evolution by natural selection in 1859.

Steps: variation exists, competition for resources, individuals with helpful alleles survive and reproduce, so those alleles increase.

If populations become isolated (e.g. a mountain), different mutations and selection pressures act on each.

Over generations they can no longer interbreed to produce fertile offspring — a new species has formed.

Useful genes are cut out with enzymes and inserted into bacteria or crops — e.g. bacterial insulin, herbicide-resistant maize.

expects you to discuss benefits and concerns — yield and medicine vs unknown ecological effects.

mcqs.q: What does it mean for an allele to be 'dominant'?
options: Organisms decide what features they need and grow them by force of will.
A dominant allele physically destroys the recessive allele in the genome.
A dominant allele is the most common allele in a population.
It is expressed in the phenotype when at least one copy is present (in a heterozygote).

mcqs.q: How does a population of organisms become better adapted to its environment over time?
options: Individual organisms change during their lifetime in response to their environment and pass the changes on to offspring.
Individuals with advantageous heritable variations survive and reproduce more; their alleles increase in frequency over generations.
